title: Percent & Percentage
tips: 10% is a one-place decimal shift; build 15% = 10% + 5%.
The base of a % change is always the OLD value.
x% of y = y% of x, so pick the easier one (8% of 50 = 50% of 8 = 4).

title: Fractions, Decimals & Operations

items.f: Parentheses → Exponents → × and ÷ (left to right) → + and − (left to right)
a/b ÷ c/d = a/b × d/c (multiply by the reciprocal)

tips: × and ÷ share one rank, so go left to right; do not multiply first.
Cancel common factors before multiplying fractions.

title: Ratio, Proportion & Sharing

items.f: a : b = c : d ⇒ a × d = b × c

items.n: Share a total in a ratio
items.f: One part = total ÷ (sum of ratio parts); each share = parts × one part
A:B = m:n and B:C = p:q ⇒ A:B:C = mp : np : nq

tips: Find the unit rate first (cost per item, km per liter), then multiply.
Subtracting the same number from both terms changes the ratio.

title: Profit, Loss & Discount

items.f: Profit = SP − CP; Loss = CP − SP
Profit % = profit ÷ CP × 100 (the base is COST)
SP = CP × (1 + profit%)  or  CP × (1 − loss%)
CP = SP ÷ (1 + profit%)  or  SP ÷ (1 − loss%)
Sale price = marked price × (1 − discount%) (the base is MARKED PRICE)

items.n: Same SP, +x% and −x% on two items
items.e: Two items sold at ₱990, +10% and −10% → 1% loss overall

tips: Markups and discounts multiply; they never add (+40% then −25% = ×1.40 × 0.75 = ×1.05).
Profit % uses cost as the base; discount % uses the marked price.

title: Simple & Compound Interest

items.f: I = P × r × t  (r as a decimal, t in years)
A = P(1 + r)ⁿ; CI = A − P

tips: 'Doubles in 4 years' means ×8 takes 3 × 4 = 12 years.
Subtract two successive amounts to get one year's interest.

title: Average, Mean & Median

items.f: Average = sum ÷ count; Sum = average × count
The average equals the middle number (odd count) or the mean of the two middle ones
Sort the values; the middle one (or the mean of the middle two)

items.n: Change in average when a value is added
items.f: New value = new total − old total

tips: Work with totals, not averages.
The average of an arithmetic sequence = (first + last) ÷ 2.

title: Speed, Distance & Time

items.f: Opposite directions: a + b;  same direction: a − b
items.e: 300 km apart, 40 and 60 km/h toward each other → 3 h
200 m train, 300 m bridge, 25 m/s → 20 s

items.f: Downstream D = b + c; upstream U = b − c;  b = (D + U) ÷ 2;  c = (D − U) ÷ 2

tips: Never average two speeds directly; the true average is closer to the slower one.
Keep units consistent: km with hours, m with seconds.

title: Work, Pipes & Man-days

items.f: Net rate = fill rate − drain rate
men × days × hours/day = constant for the same job

tips: Add rates, never times.
More workers means fewer days (inverse proportion).

title: Mixtures & Alligation

items.f: Amount of pure ingredient stays the same; new total = pure ÷ new concentration

tips: Track the part that does not change (e.g. milk when adding water).

title: Age Problems

items.f: Let the present ages be x and y; n years ago/hence is (age − n) / (age + n)
If the ratio is a : b now, ages are ax and bx; then apply the time shift to each
The difference between two ages never changes

tips: Shift ALL ages by the same number of years.
Write one equation per sentence, then solve.

title: Geometry & Mensuration

items.f: Area = l × w;  Perimeter = 2(l + w);  diagonal = √(l² + w²)
Area = ½ × b × h;  angles add to 180°
Parallelogram = b × h;  Trapezoid = ½(a + b) × h
Volume = l × w × h;  Surface area = 2(lw + lh + wh)

tips: Melting and recasting keeps volume constant: number of small solids = big volume ÷ small volume.
If a length changes by x%, area changes by the product of both length factors.

title: Number Series & Sequences

items.f: each term = sum of the previous two

tips: Look at differences first, then differences of differences, then ratios.
Also test: squares/cubes, ×2 + c, alternating patterns.

title: LCM, GCF & Divisibility

items.f: Product of the highest power of every prime in the numbers
Product of the lowest power of the common primes
For two numbers: LCM × GCF = a × b
They coincide again after the LCM of the intervals
Last digit even; last digit 0 or 5; last digit 0
Last two digits divisible by 4 / last three by 8
(sum of odd-place digits) − (sum of even-place digits) is 0 or a multiple of 11
Last digits repeat in cycles (usually 4): reduce the exponent mod 4

tips: 'Same remainder' problems → GCF of the differences.
Prime-factorize first.

title: Probability & Counting

items.f: P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A and B)
C(n, r) = n! ÷ (r! × (n − r)!)  (order does not matter)
n! ways for n different items;  repeated letters: n! ÷ (a! × b! …)

tips: Without replacement the total shrinks after every draw.
'At least one' is usually easier as 1 − P(none).
Two dice have 36 outcomes; a coin toss has 2.

title: Algebra & Exponents

items.f: (a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b²;  (a − b)² = a² − 2ab + b²
aᵐ × aⁿ = aᵐ⁺ⁿ;  aᵐ ÷ aⁿ = aᵐ⁻ⁿ;  (aᵐ)ⁿ = aᵐⁿ;  a⁰ = 1;  a⁻ⁿ = 1 ÷ aⁿ
Do the same operation to both sides to isolate x
n, n + 1, n + 2…  (odd/even: n, n + 2, n + 4…)
With h heads and f feet (2 vs 4 legs): animals with 4 legs = (f − 2h) ÷ 2

tips: Let the smallest unknown be x and express the rest in terms of it.
Plug an answer choice back in to check.
